label: copy phase: z/n/j input at final step of short sequences, outputting 1/z/j/t/u
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.013% of steps), 95% of mass in the copy phase. Nearly all activations are on copy steps where the fed-back input is z (52% of mass), n (30%) or j (12%), and the token being output next is 1, z, j, t or u (1 alone is 42% of mass). It concentrates on the last copy step (to_go==0, 65% of mass) and on short sequences (L=3-4, about half the mass); the peak is t=7, L=4. Typical top example: "c k z 1 <DEL> c k [z]". It never fires at t<3, on the delimiter, or on the first occurrence of a token in most cases (in_first=1 is only 4% of mass). Activation is fairly flat (median 0.11, max 0.18), with slightly higher values on the final step. Broad version (copy phase, input z/n/j, output in {1,z,j,t,u}) covers 80% of mass but has only 1.5% precision. The recorded tighter conjunction (final step, L<=4) reaches 23% precision and 38% recall. Even with this conjunction most matching steps stay inactive, so the feature reads a finer-grained hidden-state condition than these variables capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=5: z, n; t=7: z, n, j, 1; t=6: z) and the token being output (most: 1, z, j, t, u, e; least: k, x, c, r); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=3 & t=5, L=4 & t=7.
